name: Amelia Liu
life: “I still remember being handed the first front-door key nobody could take away.” On Tuesday, near Breakwater Way, Amelia stops on the landward side of the cycle track to watch the first boats turn for home.
voice: I grew up with no front door of my own. I'd like a shared gate I can close at night.
appearance: Amelia has silver temples and a dark fringe, one cheek that creases before the other, and a favorite piece of clothing, a long navy raincoat. It usually goes with a printed handkerchief folded into the pocket. When somebody else has the floor, Amelia holds eye contact until the other person has finished.
personality: Amelia is patient with a person learning and fiercely impatient with somebody pretending to know. A half-finished job left where a beginner can see it is an invitation, as far as Amelia is concerned.
agenda: To get a shared gate that closes securely at night.
family: Leo Hart is Amelia’s younger cousin. Amelia can always ask for five minutes alone. Leo asks before bringing somebody along. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *First shift back*, Leo says, “I was the first person they asked for advice.”
connections: Byron Sato (next-door neighbor). A locked gate can be both a new invitation and a respected boundary.

reactions.response: Amelia asks the household members who will use the garden how they want to live in it now.
